$comment: Demo dataset v2 for scripts/Load-DemoSampleData.ps1. One coherent story: the in-house legal department of Meridian Corp (fictional) runs a patent suit against Pinnacle Industries through outside counsel, renews supplier and licence agreements, answers a privacy audit and an employment dispute, and prepares an acquisition. All names, emails (example.com) and numbers are invented. Content borrowed and condensed from the spaarke-data CLI 'Meridian' scenario (C:\code_files\SPAARKE-DATA-CLI, 2026-05). Shape: every row has a stable 'key'; 'fields' are literal columns; 'dates' are day offsets from the load day; 'reference' names a taxonomy row BY NAME (data plan section 6) or an event type BY CODE; 'options' name a choice by LABEL; 'links' point at another row's key. Rules and the allowed names per section: scripts/demo-data/DemoDataLib.ps1 (Get-DemoTableSpecs) and scripts/demo-data/README.md. The loader tags every row it creates (importsequencenumber) and never writes eBilling rows (see extensionPoints).

extensionPoints.ebilling: OUT of v2 (owner decision F, 2026-11-25): invoices, budgets and billing events need the UTBMS billing codes and code sets first (data plan D5). To add them, append sections 'budgets', 'invoices' and 'billingEvents' after 'matters', add their specs to Get-DemoTableSpecs (create order: budgets, invoices, billingEvents) and their tables to the reset order, and borrow shapes from C:\code_files\SPAARKE-DATA-CLI\output\scenario-1-meridian\{budgets,invoices,billing-events}.json. Invoice-family rows are written only by the BFF's InvoiceSubmissionPersister on a real stamp (write-path I-20/I-24), so a loader that writes them directly needs an owner decision first.
extensionPoints.documentFiles: v2 documents are metadata only. Files need the BFF upload endpoints with a user token for the stamp's BFF app (scripts/demo-data/README.md, 'Documents and files'). A document row may carry sampleFile (a file under scripts/demo-data/sample-documents/) so a future upload step can pair the two; the loader ignores it today.

fields.sprk_mattername: Meridian Corp v. Pinnacle Industries - Patent Infringement
fields.sprk_matterdescription: Patent infringement action in the Northern District of California (Case No. 3:2025-cv-04892). Meridian asserts three precision-manufacturing patents against Pinnacle's AutoForge product line. Outside counsel: Baker & Associates LLP. Claim construction (Markman) ruling received; expert discovery and settlement posture are the live workstreams.

Review and renegotiate the annual supply agreement with Contoso Ltd. (version 3.2): pricing schedules, delivery commitments, liability caps and force majeure. The agreement expires in about five weeks; notice of intent to renew is due 60 days before expiry.
Cross-licensing of software patents between Meridian and Fabrikam Inc. covering patent families US-9,876,543 and US-10,234,567, with a quarterly royalty on usage metrics. Draft is in final review.

Data processing agreement with Northwind Traders under GDPR Article 28 and CCPA: controller and processor roles, data categories, security measures, breach notification timelines and sub-processor approval.

Dispute over enforcement of a non-compete clause against a former senior engineer now at Adventure Works. Covers arbitration preparation, witness statements and settlement talks. Enforceability analysis spans Washington, California and New York law.
Annual compliance audit of the Woodgrove Bank partnership agreements: OCC and FDIC requirements, BSA/AML obligations, consumer protection clauses and fair lending.
Federal registration of the AutoForge-adjacent house mark and product mark in classes 7 and 42, plus a clearance search and watch notice for confusingly similar filings.

fields.sprk_name: Email: Meridian Corp v. Pinnacle Industries - Engagement and Case Strategy
fields.sprk_subject: Meridian Corp v. Pinnacle Industries - Engagement and Case Strategy
fields.sprk_body:
Dear Sarah,

Thank you for selecting Baker & Associates to represent Meridian Corp. I want to confirm the key points of our litigation strategy. First, we will file the complaint in the Northern District of California asserting infringement of the three patents. Second, we should expect Pinnacle to assert invalidity defenses based on prior art; our initial search suggests these are manageable, but we will need a technical expert early. Third, I recommend budgeting approximately $500,000 through trial, with the expectation that settlement discussions may reduce the total.

We will provide monthly invoices and quarterly budget reviews and will schedule a strategy meeting next week to discuss the discovery plan.

Best regards,
Rachel Torres
Lead Partner, IP Litigation
Baker & Associates LLP

fields.sprk_name: Email: RE: Meridian Corp v. Pinnacle Industries - Engagement and Case Strategy
fields.sprk_subject: RE: Meridian Corp v. Pinnacle Industries - Engagement and Case Strategy
fields.sprk_body:
Rachel,

Thank you for the thorough overview. The board has approved the litigation budget of $500,000 and I have full authority to direct strategy on behalf of Meridian.

Two points from our side. James Morrison, our VP of Engineering, was directly involved in developing the patented processes and will be an excellent fact witness; he can be made available for preparation sessions on short notice. We are also particularly concerned about the AutoForge Mark III, which we believe is the clearest infringing model.

Sarah

fields.sprk_name: Email: Deposition Preparation - James Morrison
fields.sprk_body:
Sarah,

We have finalised the deposition date for James Morrison. I want to schedule three preparation sessions to make sure he is thoroughly prepared for the defense examination: (1) review of key documents and chronology, 2 hours; (2) practice questioning on technical topics, 3 hours; (3) final preparation, 2 hours.

The defense will likely focus on the development timeline, any prior art references James may have been aware of, and the technical differences between Meridian's patented processes and the prior art. Please confirm James's availability.

Best regards,
Michael Park

fields.sprk_name: Email: Settlement Posture Discussion - Confidential
fields.sprk_body:
Sarah,

Following our call yesterday, I want to memorialise our discussion on settlement posture. Based on Pinnacle's AutoForge revenue, a reasonable-royalty analysis and the strength of our claim construction positions, we believe a settlement range is supportable, but I recommend we hold off on a formal demand until after the claim construction hearing. A favourable ruling would strengthen our negotiating position.

Opposing counsel has made informal inquiries about mediation, which suggests Pinnacle may be feeling pressure. I recommend we say we are open to discussing resolution but focused on trial preparation. Please confirm you are comfortable with this approach.

Best regards,
Rachel Torres

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

fields.sprk_name: Email: Post-Markman Hearing Analysis - Confidential
fields.sprk_body:
Dear Sarah,

I am pleased to report that the claim construction hearing went very well for Meridian. Judge Sullivan construed 6 of 8 disputed claim terms in our favour. The court adopted a broad construction of 'precision alignment mechanism', the core limitation in all three asserted patents, which encompasses the full range of AutoForge implementations including the Mark III. The two terms construed in Pinnacle's favour relate to peripheral limitations.

This ruling strengthens our position for trial and settlement. I would like to schedule a call with you and the executive team to discuss next steps.

Best regards,
Rachel Torres

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL

fields.sprk_name: Email: Expert Engagement - Dr. Robert Patel
fields.sprk_body:
Dear Dr. Patel,

Thank you for agreeing to serve as plaintiff's expert in Meridian Corp v. Pinnacle Industries. We need your opinion on whether Pinnacle's AutoForge product line infringes the three asserted patents. Specifically we ask you to analyse the technical specifications of AutoForge, compare the implementation against each claim, provide a claim-by-claim analysis and prepare a written report suitable for submission to the Court.

Our target for your initial report is early next quarter. Please let us know your availability for a kickoff meeting next week.

Best regards,
Rachel Torres
Baker & Associates LLP

fields.sprk_name: Email: Contoso renewal - proposed commercial terms
fields.sprk_body:
Marcus,

Ahead of the renewal, Contoso would like to propose a move from quarterly to annual price adjustment, a 3 percent volume rebate above the agreed forecast, and a mutual cap on liability equal to twelve months of fees. We would also like to discuss extending the term to three years.

Could we set up a call this week?

Tom Alvarez
Key Account Executive, Contoso Ltd.

fields.sprk_name: Email: RE: Contoso renewal - proposed commercial terms
fields.sprk_subject: RE: Contoso renewal - proposed commercial terms
fields.sprk_body:
Tom,

Thank you. We are open to the annual price adjustment and the rebate, subject to review of the indexation clause. A mutual liability cap is acceptable in principle but we need carve-outs for confidentiality and data protection. A three-year term works if there is a termination right on 90 days' notice after year one.

Daniel Hartman of Whitfield Hartman will send a redline next week.

Marcus Webb

I recommend we prepare the Washington enforceability analysis in parallel with witness statements so we are ready for the arbitration. I will send the draft analysis by the end of next week.

Daniel Hartman
Whitfield Hartman LLP

Daniel Hartman
